text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Algeria to resumes negotiations with the European Union in April over an asscociation trade accord.

- Political parties gear up for the parliamentary elections: Abdallah Djaballah, Nahda leader, says political parties should coordinate their efforts to supervise the poll. Redha Malek, from the Repulican National Alliance, says election alliances with other parties must be forged at local level.
- Five people killed in Khemis el Kechna, southwest of Algiers, in a clash.
- Political parties await the Constitutional Council to endorse party and election laws voted by the Transitional National Council.
- National Liberation Front holds leadership meeting on Thursday to select candidates for the parliamentary elections on June 5.
- Algeria to start a 40-hour working week on March 11.
- The government adopts legislation to protect archaeological sites.
- President Liamine Zeroual meets party leaders over elections.
- Algeria to launch a diplomatic campaign to promote partnership and cooperation with its diplomatic and trade partners.
